subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I'm planning a phoenix design with spread wings in a flying pose, working out how to position the body so it still reads as grounded with the tail feathers trailing down near the floor.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a hips root joint, a spine chain curving up through the chest, a neck chain leading to the head and jaw, then figuring out how to sweep a body mesh along that spine path.

Finishing the sweep with just the spine and neck bones, I'm setting radii that taper for the body fat profile and applying a crimson-to-orange countershade gradient across back and belly. For the head, I'm planning a sphere with hooked upper and lower beak cones, amber eyes, and a flame-shaped extruded crest of plumes swept backward.

Working out the plume orientation...

Defining flame outline points...

Defining wing bone chains...

Working out the feather orientation vectors...

Attaching feather mounts to specific joints along the arm chain, using wrist, elbow, and shoulder joints for primaries, secondaries, and inner feathers respectively, and working out directional angles and lengths for the primary feathers rotating back from the outward direction.

Adding tail ribbon rigging...

Still refining ribbon geometry...

The center tail ribbon should extend longest and lowest, with side ribbons progressively shorter. For legs, I'm sketching a simple tucked-trailing chain from hip to knee to ankle, angled backward and down to suggest a bird in flight.

Adding gold spike toes at each ankle, then building the head joint attached to the end of the neck chain, oriented upward and forward.

For the head shape itself, I'm placing a scaled sphere onto the head bone slightly offset forward and up, using the bone's local-space helper for positioning. Then I'm sketching the beak as a curved sweep from head to tip, plus a separate jaw joint parented to the head for the lower mandible.

Still working out the eye placement...

For the eye glow I'll use a bright color with a glinting ring effect. Then I'm scattering 60 small octahedron embers near the wings and below in yellow/orange tones, placed via random positioning and attached to the hip bone, plus considering a crest and chest flame plumes to add extra detail.

I'm skipping the collar of flame feathers and manual chest extrudes for simplicity, instead focusing on overall proportions -- checking that the tail tip, crest height, and wingspan feel right for a mythical phoenix scale, then confirming the lowest points (tail and talons) sit correctly, and double-checking how the random number generator function is meant to be called.

I'm writing a safe wrapper that handles either a callable rng or an object with a .next() method, then building a feather paint function that colors each feather crimson or another hue based on its position along the length.

Writing the extrude helper...

I need to fix the mirroring so the outline's y-direction always points backward regardless of which side it's flipped to — just negate yv when its z-component is positive, keeping the flame's curved trailing edge consistent. Then I'm thinking about keeping the feathers thin.

For origins, each primary feather should root at the wrist point (with slight x-spread), nudged toward the elbow for the inner ones using a small lerp factor. I'm noticing the arm's rising slope from shoulder to wrist (~23°) doesn't match the feather plane's tilt (~11°), so I need to adjust the normal vector to compensate.

I'm computing the normalized tilt (~22°) and checking feather sweep directions against it—both the upward-tilting and backward-sweeping primaries check out consistently. For secondary feathers, I'm placing their origins by lerping along the straight arm segments (shoulder-to-elbow and elbow-to-wrist), binding each to the appropriate joint in a three-joint chain: shoulder, elbow, and wrist tip.

Primaries attach to the wrist joint, with coverts layered slightly above using a raised offset and a paint gradient so the topmost ones shift toward orange while most stay crimson. I'm sweeping the arm as a tube using crimson coloring along the rigid chain, deciding the shoulder sphere is unnecessary since the body radius already covers it, and skipping extra flourishes like chest plumes or a glow halo. For the tail, I'm setting up a ribbon chain parented to the hips with four uniquely named segments.

Working through the tail ribbon naming to avoid collisions, then calculating each ribbon's path points based on its index -- computing a spread factor, length scaling, and endpoint positions so the ribbons fan outward and droop naturally from the hips.

Skipping flame tips at ribbon ends for now, and setting body colors with countershading between crimson and orange, with the head in a distinct orange-red tone.

Now I'm placing the crest plumes at the top of the head, positioning seven plumes at varying angles and lateral offsets to create a swept-back crest effect, computing their lengths accordingly.

Working out the plume orientation vectors...

Deciding crest colors per segment and adding plume details, then defining the head joint position from the end of the neck path. I'm laying out body path points for the spine and neck curve, pitched slightly upward and forward, splitting it into spine and neck slices with assigned radii.

Still placing joints... figuring out the head sphere position and direction at the neck's end, then setting shoulder joints on the body surface for the wing chain parented to the spine, and hip joints for the legs parented to the hips, with left/right side naming for symmetric limbs.

Now I'm sketching the ember particles scattered around the wing area—small octahedron shapes in warm yellow-orange tones, avoiding low altitudes—plus defining the wing and leg bone chains with role tags and setting up a helper for building the feather shapes along each wing.

Defining feather outline points...

Still working out feather geometry...

To fix z-fighting between overlapping coplanar primaries, I'll nudge each one slightly along the normal using an index-based offset. Then I'm sketching the beak structure, building the lower jaw as a spike shape anchored between points on the head mesh.

Adding upper beak with a small hook formed from a second spike connecting to the lower tip, making sure the jaw bone exists before referencing it. Now writing the final version.
